articles.title: A cinco dias das eleições, governo lança Desenrola MEI e novas medidas de renegociação de dívidas | G1
articles.standfirst: Pacote de medidas é voltado a MEIs, produtores rurais, pessoas físicas, empregadores e ex-bolsistas de pesquisa.
articles.summary: Pacote de medidas é voltado a MEIs, produtores rurais, pessoas físicas, empregadores e ex-bolsistas de pesquisa.
articles.body:
A cinco dias das eleições, o governo federal anunciou nesta terça-feira (29) um pacote de medidas destinadas à renegociação de dívidas de microempreendedores individuais (MEIs), produtores rurais, pessoas físicas, empregadores e ex-bolsistas de pesquisa.

As iniciativas incluem a criação de novos programas de transação tributária e a prorrogação de editais já existentes para negociação de débitos federais.

Pelo lado da Procuradoria-Geral da Fazenda Nacional (PGFN), foi lançado o Desenrola MEI Pequeno Valor, voltado a microempreendedores com débitos de até cinco salários mínimos, ou seja, R$ 8.105.

🗓️ A janela de renegociação poderá ser feita entre 1º de outubro de 2026 e 31 de janeiro de 2027 .

O programa prevê entrada de 5% do valor da dívida, sem desconto, e parcelamento do saldo restante em até 55 meses, com abatimento de 50%.

💰A PGFN também abriu uma modalidade de negociação voltada a empregadores pessoas físicas e jurídicas com passivo consolidado de até R$ 45 milhões em débitos inscritos em dívida ativa do FGTS ou da União.

Empresas incluídas no cadastro de empregadores que submeteram trabalhadores a condições análogas à escravidão não são contemplados.

🗓️ Além das novas medidas, o governo prorrogou até 29 de janeiro de 2027 três programas já em vigor.

Entre eles está o edital de transação destinado a pessoas físicas e jurídicas com dívidas de até R$ 45 milhões inscritas em dívida ativa até 3 de março de 2026, ou até 1º de junho de 2025 nos casos classificados como de pequeno valor.

Segundo o governo, os descontos podem chegar a 100% sobre juros, multas e encargos legais, mas não incidem sobre o valor principal da dívida. O abatimento total fica limitado a 65% do débito consolidado.

Para pessoas físicas, MEIs, microempresas, empresas de pequeno porte, cooperativas e Santas Casas, o limite pode alcançar 70%.

Os programas Desenrola MEI e Desenrola Rural também tiveram o prazo de adesão prorrogado até 29 de janeiro de 2027 .

Prazo para renegociar dívidas no Desenrola Brasil termina nesta segunda (20) — Foto: Luis Lima Jr./Fotoarena/Estadão Conteúdo

Pelo lado da Advocacia-Geral da União (AGU), foi anunciado ainda um edital específico para MEIs que possuem débitos de até cinco salários mínimos junto a autarquias e fundações públicas federais .

De acordo com o governo, cerca de 10 mil devedores poderão ser beneficiados pela iniciativa, que envolve um volume estimado de R$ 50 milhões em débitos .

A AGU também lançou duas modalidades para ex-bolsistas da Coordenação de Aperfeiçoamento de Pessoal de Nível Superior (Capes) e do Conselho Nacional de Desenvolvimento Científico e Tecnológico (CNPq) com dívidas relacionadas a bolsas de estudo no Brasil ou no exterior.

O prazo para adesão vai de 16 de outubro de 2026 a 31 de março de 2027 . Os descontos variam conforme a forma de pagamento e podem chegar a 70% para quitação à vista e a 30% para parcelamentos em até 84 meses.

O desconto é sobre o valor consolidado do crédito, incluídos o principal, os juros, as multas e os encargos legais, mas não poderá resultar em valor inferior ao montante principal do crédito.

articles.title: Globo anuncia finalistas do Prêmio Profissionais do Ano 2026 | G1
articles.standfirst: Em sua 48ª edição, a premiação reúne 79 trabalhos finalistas em 17 categorias, selecionados entre mais de 850 peças inscritas em todo o país.
articles.summary: Premiação chega à 48ª edição com 79 trabalhos finalistas em 17 categorias; foram mais de 850 peças inscritas em todo o país.
articles.body:
Prêmio Profissionais do Ano (PPA) 2026 — Foto: Divulgação

O Prêmio Profissionais do Ano (PPA) 2026 anunciou, nesta terça-feira (29), os finalistas da edição . Ao todo, são 79 trabalhos distribuídos em 17 categorias , selecionados entre mais de 850 peças inscritas em todo o país.

Em sua 48ª edição, a premiação reúne trabalhos de diferentes regiões, formatos e estilos de comunicação. Neste ano, o prêmio também inclui uma categoria voltada a estudantes, em parceria com a Academia LED Globo.

Para Manzar Feres, diretora-geral de Negócios da Globo, a diversidade de olhares é uma das características da criatividade brasileira que se destacam nesta edição.

“O PPA reconhece ideias que entendem o jeito brasileiro de viver, falar e se relacionar com o mundo, transformando mobilização em negócios. Nesta edição, essa visão está presente no conceito ‘Ideia boa fala brasileiro’ e na chegada dos estudantes ao prêmio, por meio da parceria com a Academia LED Globo”, afirma.

“Entendemos que precisamos nos conectar com esses novos profissionais, trocar com eles, compartilhar nosso conhecimento, mas também aprender. Celebrar a criatividade é também investir no futuro dela”, acrescenta.

Na classe Regional, os trabalhos concorrem nas categorias Filme e Campanha, divididas entre as regiões Sul, Sudeste Capital, Sudeste Interior, Norte-Nordeste e Leste-Oeste. ( veja quem são os finalistas )

A classe Nacional reúne as categorias Filme 30, Filme 30+, Campanha, Ações em Conteúdo, Integrada e Valor Social. Na categoria Integrada, também passam a ser considerados trabalhos exibidos nas telas da Eletromídia.

articles.title: Brasil cria 165,8  mil empregos com carteira assinada em agosto, aponta Caged | G1
articles.standfirst: Resultado representa uma alta em relação a agosto de 2025 — quando foram criados 154.827 mil empregos com carteira assinada.
articles.summary: Resultado representa uma alta em relação a agosto de 2025 — quando foram criados 154.827 mil empregos com carteira assinada.
articles.body:
A economia brasileira gerou 165.827 mil empregos formais em agosto deste ano , informou nesta terça-feira (29) o Ministério do Trabalho e do Emprego.

Ao todo, segundo o governo federal, foram registradas em agosto:

📈 O resultado representa uma alta em relação a agosto de 2025 — quando foram criados 154.827 mil empregos com carteira assinada.

De acordo com o Ministério do Trabalho, 1.134.033 milh de empregos formais foram criados no país de janeiro a agosto deste ano.

O número representa queda de 25,2% na comparação com o mesmo período de 2025 , quando foram abertas 1,516 milhão de vagas com carteira assinada.

Já com relação aos últimos 12 meses, o saldo também ficou positivo, com a criação de 887,7 mil empregos formais, crescimento de 1,87%. O estoque total chegou a 48,24 milhões de vínculos formais.

Brasil cria 165,8 mil empregos com carteira assinada em agosto, aponta Caged — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

Os números do Cadastro Geral de Empregados e Desempregados (Caged) de agosto de 2026 mostram que foram criados empregos formais em cinco setores da economia.

Dentro do setor de Serviços, os principais destaques foram Educação, com a criação de 25,4 mil postos; Saúde e serviços sociais, com 19,1 mil; e Transporte, Armazenagem e Correio, com 16,8 mil vagas.

“A gente viu uma recuperação do mercado varejista, e a indústria manteve um crescimento que vem de alguns meses, um crescimento mais estruturado. A construção civil mantém esse aquecimento, com salário de entrada mais elevado. A gente vê um movimento da economia”, afirmou Chico Macena, ministro do Trabalho em exercício.

Os dados também revelam que foram abertas vagas em 24 das 27 unidades federativas, com destaque, em valores absolutos, para São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro e Pernambuco.

Já em termos relativos, Paraíba, Amapá e Rio Grande do Norte.

O governo também informou que o salário médio real de admissão foi de R$ 2.410,74 em agosto, queda de 0,03% em relação a julho. Na comparação com agosto de 2025, houve alta real de 1,02%.

Na comparação com agosto do ano passado, também houve aumento no salário médio de admissão. Naquele mês, o valor foi de R$ 2.386,43.

Os dados do Cadastro Geral de Empregados e Desempregados consideram os trabalhadores com carteira assinada, ou seja, não incluem os informais.

Com isso, os resultados não são comparáveis com os números do desemprego divulgados pelo Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística ( IBGE ), coletados por meio da Pesquisa Nacional por Amostra de Domicílios Continua (Pnad).

Segundo dados oficiais, a taxa de desemprego no Brasil ficou em 5,3% no trimestre encerrado em agosto deste ano. Os dados são da Pesquisa Nacional por Amostra de Domicílios (PNAD) Contínua, divulgada nesta terça-feira (29) pelo Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE).

O resultado representa uma queda de 0,3 ponto percentual (p.p.) tanto em relação aos três meses encerrados em maio quanto na comparação com o mesmo período de 2025 — ambos com taxas de 5,6%.

articles.title: Justiça derruba restrições da 99Food a restaurantes que usam Keeta | G1
articles.standfirst: Decisão do TJ-SP vale em todo o país; 99Food afirma que acordos eram voluntários e diz que vai recorrer.
articles.summary: Decisão do TJ-SP vale em todo o país; 99Food afirma que acordos eram voluntários e diz que vai recorrer.
articles.body:
Capacete inteligente será disponibilizado pela Keeta inicialmente para ciclistas e, posteriormente, para motociclistas. — Foto: Divulgação

O Tribunal de Justiça de São Paulo (TJ-SP) derrubou as cláusulas de banimento impostas pela 99Food a restaurantes para impedir que os estabelecimentos trabalhassem com a Keeta , de acordo com comunicado da empresa chinesa à imprensa nesta terça-feira (29).

A decisão, tomada por unanimidade, tem validade em todo o território nacional.

A Keeta, braço internacional da chinesa Meituan, iniciou as operações no Brasil em 2025 e entrou com uma ação contra a 99Food no mesmo ano.

"Acreditamos que esta decisão fortalecerá todo o ecossistema, garantindo um mercado de delivery livre de cláusulas anticompetitivas em benefício de todos", disse o vice-presidente da Keeta no Brasil, Danilo Mansano.

A 99Food afirmou que o julgamento se baseou em uma compreensão equivocada dessas cláusulas e de seus objetivos.

"Os acordos, celebrados voluntariamente pelos restaurantes e por prazo limitado, permitem que uma plataforma entrante, como a 99Food, construa a escala necessária de restaurantes, consumidores e entregadores parceiros para se estabelecer no mercado e desafiar um agente dominante no setor", disse a empresa.

A 99Food destacou que a decisão não encerra o processo e será objeto dos recursos cabíveis.

Aplicativo 99 — Foto: Bruno Peres/Agência Brasil

articles.title: TV Rio Sul debate novas estratégias de publicidade regional  | G1
articles.standfirst: Encontro reuniu profissionais para apresentar soluções integradas de mídia e projetos voltados aos anunciantes da região.
articles.summary: O encontro Café & Negócios da TV Rio Sul reuniu profissionais para apresentar soluções de mídia integrada e novas estratégias de comunicação para o mercado regional.
articles.body:
TV Rio Sul realiza ‘Café & Negócios’ para debater comunicação e estratégias publicitárias na região. — Foto: Divulgação/Tv Rio Sul

A TV Rio Sul realizou nesta terça-feira (29), em Volta Redonda (RJ) mais uma edição do encontro ''Café & Negócios''. A reunião contou com profissionais da área da publicidade para discutir novas possibilidades de comunicação e estratégias voltadas ao mercado na região.

A iniciativa é voltada para compartilhar novidades do mercado publicitário e explorar caminhos estratégicos para o desenvolvimento de campanhas na região.

Durante o encontro, foram apresentadas soluções que integram diferentes plataformas de conteúdo, como televisão aberta, os portais g1 e ge e o serviço de streaming Globoplay para mostrar como diferentes canais podem ser utilizados de forma integrada nas campanhas.

O encontro também abordou diferentes formatos comerciais, incluindo ações de mídia, patrocínios e projetos personalizados, alinhados com os objetivos dos anunciantes.

O “Café & Negócios” busca aproximar empresas e profissionais do setor para discutir estratégias e oportunidades de comunicação no mercado regional.

articles.title: Transações com PIX caem 10% após proibição das bets; veja os dados | G1
articles.standfirst: Dados do Banco Central mostram 608,6 milhões de transações entre sábado e segunda-feira, volume 10% menor que a média dos mesmos dias nas quatro semanas anteriores.
articles.summary: Dados do Banco Central mostram 608,6 milhões de transações entre sábado e segunda-feira, volume 10% menor que a média dos mesmos dias nas quatro semanas anteriores.
articles.body:
O número de transações com PIX caiu cerca de 10% nos três dias seguintes à publicação da medida provisória (MP) que proíbe as apostas esportivas online, conhecidas como "bets". A medida foi publicada na sexta-feira (25) .

Segundo dados do Banco Central sobre as operações liquidadas no Sistema de Pagamentos Instantâneos (SPI), foram registradas 229,6 milhões de transações no sábado (26), queda de 11% em relação à média dos quatro sábados anteriores.

No domingo (27), foram 165,9 milhões de transações, redução de 12% na mesma comparação. Na segunda-feira (28), dado mais recente disponível, foram 213 milhões , queda de 7,4% em relação à média das quatro segundas-feiras anteriores.

No acumulado dos três dias, foram 608,6 milhões de transações, volume 10% menor que a média registrada no mesmo intervalo das quatro semanas anteriores.

Transações com PIX recuam depois da proibição das bets — Foto: Arte/g1

➡️ Os números fazem parte das estatísticas do Sistema de Pagamentos Instantâneos (SPI) divulgadas pelo Banco Central. A base reúne as transações PIX liquidadas no sistema.

O g1 questionou o Banco Central sobre uma eventual relação entre a queda das transações e a publicação da MP que proíbe as bets e sobre se os dados disponíveis permitem estabelecer essa associação.

Até a última atualização desta reportagem, o Banco Central não havia respondido.

Órgãos de defesa do consumidor do Espírito Santo querem que bets sejam obrigadas a informar risco de perda para apostadores. — Foto: Arquivo/Agência Brasil

articles.title: Inside McDonald’s push to have AI price your Big Mac
articles.summary: By Waylon Cunningham NEW YORK, Sept 29 (Reuters) - McDonald’s is increasingly using artificial intelligence to guide menu prices across the U.S. and some glo...
articles.body:
NEW YORK, Sept 29 (Reuters) - McDonald's is increasingly using artificial intelligence to guide menu prices across the U.S. and some global markets, a plan that aims to boost headquarters' profit but risks alienating customers and attracting antitrust scrutiny.

One pricing factor supercharged by AI: an estimate of how much each store's patrons are willing to pay.

The details of how that pricing system works, its extensive use of AI, the company's regulatory concerns and the tensions with its franchisees haven't been previously reported. For this story, Reuters reviewed screenshots of the company pricing engine taken in August and interviewed nine sources with first-hand knowledge of the burger chain's strategy.

McDonald's pricing ‌engine uses machine-learning algorithms to continually analyze data from millions of daily transactions across McDonald's nearly 14,000 restaurants and generate what the company calls "the optimal price" at each location for each menu item, from Big Macs to discounted coffee for seniors.

The engine has widened existing price differences for the same product between restaurants, including from neighborhood to neighborhood within ‌the same area, three franchisees told Reuters.

Screenshots of the interface franchisees use, reviewed by Reuters, show messages including: "Your restaurant is showing MEDIUM SENSITIVITY to Price" based in part on "customer willingness to pay in your area." The platform also contains public price information pulled from online menus of nearby restaurants of competitors including Wendy's and Burger King. Those chains said they do not use AI in pricing decisions.

A Reuters check of prices in September on the McDonald's mobile app showed price differences. For example, ​a company-run store in Fresno, California sells a Big Mac for $5.69, but another company-run restaurant two miles away sells the same sandwich for $6.89, a 21% premium. Reuters could not confirm if the price difference is the result of the price engine's recommendations or other factors.

McDonald's says its franchisees are free to set their own prices, but five store owners told Reuters the company pressured them to use the AI-pricing tools. A franchisee document from June reviewed by Reuters shows McDonald's records franchisees' deviations from the recommendations in detail.

In January, McDonald's started requiring franchisees to be "constructively engaging with McDonald's approved Pricing Consultant and Tools" as part of its new business standards, according to an internal communication sent to franchisees and reviewed by Reuters.

images.caption: McDonald's logo is seen in this illustration taken August 5, 2025. REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Illustration · Reuters

articles.title: Mortgage rates hit 7.58%, approaching 3-year high
articles.summary: Mortgage rates closed in on 7.6% Tuesday as Treasury yields continued to move higher.
articles.body:
Mortgage rates closed in on 7.6% Tuesday as Treasury yields continued to move higher.

The average 30-year fixed-rate mortgage rate hit 7.58% on Tuesday, per Mortgage News Daily. That's up 8 basis points from Monday, and is the highest level since November 2023.

The 10-year Treasury yield ( ^TNX ), which mortgage rates closely track, was up around 4 basis points to 5.28% as of midday.

Rates remain some distance from late 2023's peak around 7.8% — though not terribly far off — and could easily be enough to chill home sales ahead of the market's typical winter slowdown.

Sitting at 6.75% on Aug. 26, mortgage rates crossed the 7% threshold around Sept. 10 and have continued rising amid the volatility in bond markets, driven by growing investor concern about oil prices , inflation , and future Federal Reserve rate hike s .

Claire Boston is a senior reporter for Yahoo Finance covering housing, mortgages, and home insurance.

articles.title: Flipkart adds 14 mn cubic feet of storage ahead of festive sale
articles.summary: Flipkart’s Ekart adds 14 mn cu ft warehouse space, boosting storage 50% and processing 30% ahead of Big Billion Days; expands deliveries to 750+ PIN codes.
articles.body: Bengaluru: Flipkart’s logistics arm Ekart has added 14 million cubic feet of warehouse space ahead of its Big Billion Days sale, increasing its storage capacity by 50%, the company said. It has also extended deliveries to more than 750 additional PIN codes as it prepares for the festive shopping rush.Technology and automation upgrades have raised Ekart’s peak order-processing capacity by more than 30%, according to Flipkart. The company has added over 900 delivery hubs to handle higher volumes of same-day and next-day orders. Across Ekart and its quick-commerce service Flipkart Minutes, Flipkart said it now operates more than 8,200 facilities. Minutes has nearly 1,200 small fulfilment centres in over 150 cities.The new delivery locations include Leh and Kargil in Ladakh, parts of Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh, and towns across the Northeast. Hemant Badri, senior vice-president and head of supply chain at Flipkart Group, said customers in Leh and Kargil would be able to shop during Big Billion Days for the first time.Flipkart has placed more than 2.5 crore products from small businesses, weavers and artisans in Ekart fulfilment centres ahead of the sale. It has opened 70 additional pickup stations for sellers. Ekart’s franchise network, which also serves businesses outside the Flipkart marketplace, has doubled to 600 in two months, the company said.Flipkart has separately announced more than 2.5 lakh direct and indirect work opportunities for the festive season, including nearly 75,000 for people entering the workforce for the first time. articles.title: OpenAI debuts Dots AI agents in challenge to Meta's popular Muse agent
articles.summary: OpenAI debuted its Dots AI agent at its DevDay 2026.
articles.body:
OpenAI ( OPAI.PVT ) CEO Sam Altman launched the company's newest product during its OpenAI DevDay on Tuesday: Dots. A high-powered AI agent, Dots is designed to perform tasks for you over long periods via connections to 4,000 apps via ChatGPT.

For instance, you can tell your Dot to keep you updated on projects you're working on, add items to your schedule, and more.

Powered by OpenAI's Astra model, the company says Dots can do things like recognize when an alert about a software bug comes in via Slack and begin digging into it. In another example, OpenAI says an early tester's Dot saw that they didn't submit an invoice for a publication. The Dot then set up the invoice and submitted it after getting the tester's approval.

You'll also be able to hand off tasks in Slack to your Dot, helping to cut down on the ever-growing number of pings and distractions you receive each day.

According to OpenAI, users will start with a single Dot, name it and customize it for themselves. The company says that in the future, it imagines users having whole teams of Dots working together for them.

Dots will roll out to Pro, Business Premium, and Enterprise users in available markets.

OpenAI's Dots comes weeks after Meta ( META ) debuted its popular Muse AI agent . Muse quickly shot to the top of both Apple's App Store and Google's Play Store, becoming a major win for the company, as it continues to spend billions on its AI buildout.

Unlike Meta, which is marketing Muse toward the consumer market, OpenAI is angling for the enterprise space.

I've spent significant time using Meta's Muse and have found that, while it makes mistakes at times, it's generally a solid AI agent for the average person, especially for tasks like comparing products and getting quick answers to complex questions.

Dots come as OpenAI and rivals Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ), Meta, and Google ( GOOG , GOOGL ) have revealed that their various AI agents have gone rogue, hacking into various organizations and governments over the last year.

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has called on AI labs to slow the development of frontier models. Something Altman said he agreed with.

In addition to launching Dots, OpenAI unveiled its latest model, GPT-6.1 Sol.

According to the company, 6.1 Sol is nearly as powerful as its top-of-the-line Astra model for coding, computer use, and professional work, at a significantly lower price.

Pricing has become increasingly important for AI labs as customers seek ways to reduce their AI usage across their businesses.

articles.title: The job market looks steady. Underneath, hiring intentions are stirring.
articles.summary: Two new reports reveal whats under the data of today's job market.
articles.body:
With lots of numbers rolling out on the job market this week detailing hiring, firing, and job openings , two new reports reveal what's simmering underneath the surface.

Amid a long-running 'low hire, low fire' job market, Indeed found that annual growth in job postings has turned positive for the first time since 2022, according to new research .

"Our data shows hiring intentions rising slightly, but it's unclear if those intentions will turn to action," Cory Stahle, a senior economist at Indeed, told Yahoo Finance.

His take: The number of jobs added in a given month, whether up or down, is ultimately a function of employers' hiring appetite and workers' willingness to take a risk on a new opportunity.

Postings in software development and data and analytics, two areas that had pulled back sharply in recent times, are adding postings again.

For the most part, unemployment is low, wages are generally flat, and people are holding onto their jobs.

That doesn't make things easy for those hunting for a job.

"They're competing for fewer roles, which helps explain why so many job seekers feel stuck," said Laura Ullrich, director of economic research at the Indeed Hiring Lab.

Meanwhile, economists project the unemployment rate will hold steady at 4.1% in September 2026 and rise only slightly next year.

What that means for workers is debatable. A 4.1% rate today says something very different about labor dynamics than it has historically, due to population changes.

The US labor force has shrunk by around 700,000 workers so far in 2026. "Absent a surprise fourth-quarter shift, 2026 will be just the second time since 1948 that we've seen a shrinking labor force outside of a recession," per Ullrich.

Combined with baby boomers retiring, the dwindling labor supply makes it mathematically less likely for the unemployment rate to increase, she said.

For decades, there have been ominous warnings about the demographic cliff due to falling birth rates, translating to fewer younger workers to replace older workers hitting the exits.

It's arriving now, but it's not just older workers stepping out of the workplace. It's across all age groups when you factor in the drop in immigration and fewer women in the workforce.

"The United States is likely entering a period where hires and payroll employment will be lower than we've grown to expect — not because of limited demand, but because there simply aren't enough workers to fill available jobs," according to Ullrich.

articles.title: TrumpRx promises some of the world's lowest drug prices. Does it deliver?
articles.summary: TrumpRx offers discounted prices on prescription drugs, but the platform still charges more than in other countries for some medications, a new analysis show...
articles.body:
Some offers on this page are from advertisers who pay us, which may affect which products we write about, but not our recommendations. See our Advertiser Disclosure .

When the Trump administration launched TrumpRx in early 2026, it promised to "ensure Americans pay prices aligned with the lowest in other developed nations, ending decades of overpayment and delivering immediate relief."

But a new analysis from KFF shows that the results, so far, are mixed.

The nonpartisan health policy research, polling, and news organization's report analyzed 32 brand-name drugs without generics listed on TrumpRx that had publicly available prices in comparable "peer" countries, including Australia, Canada, France, Germany, Japan, the United Kingdom, and more.

For 17 of the 32 drugs, the TrumpRx price was lower than the average price in other countries. But for the remaining 15 drugs, the TrumpRx price was higher than the average price in other countries. And 13 have higher prices on TrumpRx than in any other country included in the comparison.

"There's no across-the-board pattern of higher prices for brand-name drugs listed on TrumpRx compared to other countries, but there's also no consistent pattern of lower prices," said Juliette Cubanski, vice president and director of the program on Medicare policy at KFF.

"The takeaway, I think, for patients is that there's no guarantee that the price they will face for a given brand-name drug on TrumpRx is lower than what the drug's price would be in another country."

There are some caveats to keep in mind. The KFF analysis used publicly listed prices from other countries, which don't necessarily reflect the out-of-pocket costs for patients in those countries who use their available healthcare systems.

TrumpRx "continues to deliver measurable savings for American patients nationwide, in many cases offering drugs at prices below the average prices paid in comparable developed countries," a representative from the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services said in a statement to Yahoo Finance, citing $700 million in prescription drug savings for Americans through the program.

TrumpRx prices compared to other countries

The rising cost of prescription drugs in America isn't new.

AARP also published a report in May showing that prices for some brand-name drugs have increased in the U.S. while decreasing in other countries. In an analysis of 25 brand-name drugs, AARP found that U.S. list prices had increased by an average of 81% since the drugs entered the market, while prices across 19 other "high-income countries" decreased by an average of 13%.

The report also acknowledged that "efforts are underway to address this longstanding issue," including the administration's push to lower drug prices for Americans through "Most Favored Nation" pricing.

The lower costs for brand-name drugs on the TrumpRx platform are available through "Most Favored Nation" price agreements with drug manufacturers, and brand-name drugs with "Most Favored Nation" pricing are listed on TrumpRx as "Presidential deals." In May, the site also began listing hundreds of generic drug prices, and more prescription medications are continually being added.

In August, the Trump administration reported that prescription drug prices showed their largest annual decline in over 60 years, citing Bureau of Labor Statistics data.

KFF's analysis, however, shows that not all patients are seeing the same price declines in comparison to other countries. Of the 32 drugs analyzed, five were listed for the lowest price on TrumpRx compared to the other countries. TrumpRx charged the highest price among the other countries for 13 of the brand-name drugs, though.

KFF's analysis did not compare the costs Americans are paying now to what they paid for the same drugs before the platform launched.

"Prescription drug affordability remains a serious concern for millions of Americans, and there is still significant work to do to bring down prices," said Leigh Purvis, prescription drug policy principal at AARP, in a statement to Yahoo Finance. "We always recommend comparing your options."

How to find the best deals on prescription medications

Comparing prices from multiple available options can help you get the best price for your prescription medications. TrumpRx is one resource, but there are other actions you can take too.

You can look into other discount programs, compare different pharmacy options in your area or online, talk to your doctor about generic equivalents, and more.

"Shop around," Michelle Long, senior policy manager for the Program on Patient and Consumer Protections at KFF, previously said to Yahoo Finance . "Check what all of your options might be, both for paying cash and for using your health insurance."

TrumpRx is generally useful for people without insurance coverage or those who want access to brand-name drugs their plan doesn't cover. Those who want access to GLP-1s for weight loss or fertility drugs, for example, may often find savings on TrumpRx when they can't get the drugs through insurance.

The math often looks different when insurance applies for a drug, however. In most cases, insurance co-pays are going to cost less than the discounted price through TrumpRx. The TrumpRx site even recommends users check their insurance co-pays before paying cash: "Insured patients should always check the TrumpRx price against those offered through their insurance companies."

There are other sites where you can find coupons for discounted prescription drugs, like GoodRx and Mark Cuban's Cost Plus Drugs.

These sites can all work a bit differently. TrumpRx typically shows you different in-person and delivery pharmacy options. You can choose the one that's best for you, then ask your doctor to send the prescription there. With Cost Plus Drugs, you'll need to create an account on the site and have your doctor send your prescription to the platform, which will mail it to you.

Each may offer different prices and instructions for receiving your medication. The medications they offer can also differ.

"It really does boil down to using TrumpRx as a way to shop around on the prices of medications, but I don't think people can assume that they'll be paying the lowest price for the medication if they use the Trump Rx website," Cubanski said.

TrumpRx expands discount drug offerings: What consumers should know

How TrumpRx may help you save money on prescription drugs — and other ways to lower the cost of your medications.

Paying cash for healthcare could help cut your medical bills

With discounts of up to 80% on medical costs, it's becoming increasingly difficult not to consider cash-pay healthcare.

FDA approves first-of-its-kind cholesterol pill Lipfendra: What it will cost

The daily medication is expected to be list-priced at $10.50 per pill. Here's what to know about Merck's new cholesterol drug Lipfendra.

Medicare will cover GLP-1 weight-loss drugs for $50 per month. How you could save.

Medicare beneficiaries can get GLP-1s for $50 per month through a temporary program called Bridge. Here’s how to determine if you’re eligible.

Medicare changes coming in 2027: What to know before open enrollment

Some Medicare costs for 2027 aren’t final yet, but the latest government forecasts offer a clearer picture of what beneficiaries can expect.

Trump Accounts could help lower-income families most. Few have signed up.

Some eligible families are still uncertain whether Trump Accounts are right for their children, which keeps them from taking advantage of the account's benefits.

articles.title: AI agents are coming to your home and office
articles.summary: OpenAI and Meta are bringing AI agents to the masses.
articles.body:
If you're not using an AI agent now, chances are you may be in the near future.

On Tuesday, OpenAI ( OPAI.PVT) CEO Sam Altman debuted the company's new Dots AI agent platform . Designed to handle mundane tasks, like helping arrange your work schedule, as well as more complex operations, such as making purchases on your behalf or reviewing code, Dots is just the latest AI agent to hit the increasingly crowded space.

Earlier this month, Meta ( META ) unveiled its Muse agent . The app quickly shot to the top of both Apple's App Store and Google's Play Store.

While Dots and Muse are intended for different audiences — OpenAI is initially positioning Dots for the enterprise space, while Meta is angling for the consumer market — the pair share one key similarity: They feature cute, customizable looks meant to make them appear more approachable. And that could drive adoption both in users' personal lives and in the office.

Powered by OpenAI's Astra model , Dots can triage Slack notifications , prepare invoices, and more. In a prepared demonstration, OpenAI showed how Dots can recognize when you have work scheduled through dinner, then pull up delivery options and place an order for you with your permission.

Meta's Muse, which I've been using , has helped me parse my Verizon Wireless bill and compare it to competing offerings from AT&T and T-Mobile, search for movers, and set up breaking news alerts for the latest tech headlines.

The agents are a means to help companies move beyond traditional chatbots into a world where AI completes work for you.

Agents aren't exactly new. I previously dubbed 2025 the year of the AI agent amid big talk about the technology from companies like Microsoft (MSFT), Nvidia (NVDA), Google ( GOOG , GOOGL ), and others. Earlier this year, OpenClaw took the tech world by storm thanks to its ability to run AI agents on users' personal computers.

The latest push from Meta and OpenAI comes as AI agents gain greater capabilities thanks to more powerful underlying models.

But that's also led to a deluge of hacking incidents over the summer from leading AI companies, including OpenAI and Meta. This week, OpenAI said it is pausing the release of its Astra 6.1 model over safety concerns.

Earlier this month, Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ) CEO Dario Amodei called on AI companies to slow the development of frontier models. Altman said he agreed at the time.

Email Daniel Howley at dhowley@yahoofinance.com. Follow him on Twitter at @DanielHowley .

articles.title: Trump gathers with AI leaders, floats 'self-regulation' as the way to deal with the technology's dangers
articles.summary: President Trump gathered top AI leaders in Washington on Tuesday and doubled down on his opposition to any government intervention, suggesting that "self-reg...
articles.body:
President Trump gathered top artificial intelligence leaders in Washington on Tuesday and doubled down on his opposition to government intervention, suggesting that "self-regulation" is the answer to growing worries about the technology getting out of human control.

"There's a belief that there should be tremendous self-regulation," the president said after meeting with the assembled CEOs. "There was a lot of commonality in this room."

Trump said he and the CEOs signed a "morally binding" accord that would keep the companies in line through "self-policing and group policing."

Trump posted a copy of the accord to his Truth Social account with a one-page document that called for each participating company to implement four different measures to safeguard the technology and added that, later on, "it might make sense to codify these steps into laws or regulations."

Some executives on hand said the accord included commitments to a combination of technological controls to detect problems with new models, internal risk review efforts, external auditors, and other measures.

Meta ( META ) CEO Mark Zuckerberg called the accord "a start," while others suggested some details still needed to be worked out.

"The mechanism, how we address those risks, is still under discussion," Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ) CEO Dario Amodei said. Progress had been made toward both the US winning AI and also winning safely, he said, though he emphasized that the technology still poses "real dangers."

Amodei published an essay earlier this month titled "We Must Pace the Frontier," which set off a fierce debate about the need for a cooperative slowdown in AI capability.

The accord also formally changed the name of the technology in government record-keeping to Super Intelligence.

"We've changed the name officially to SI," Trump said.

The "meeting and luncheon on Super Intelligence," as the White House described the event, took place in the East Room, with Trump even posting the seating chart . The location was the same spot where just a few days ago, many of the same AI leaders gathered for a state dinner for Chinese President Xi Jinping.

Elon Musk of Tesla ( TSLA ), Jensen Huang of Nvidia ( NVDA ), and Lisa Su of Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ) were all at the head table with Xi last Thursday and again received prominent spots near Trump.

After the meeting, Trump also said he was "very close" to a decision on an AI czar and would announce it in the next three to four days.

Other notable guests included Google ( GOOGL , GOOG ) CEO Sundar Pichai, Microsoft ( MSFT ) CEO Satya Nadella, OpenAI ( OPAI.PVT ) president Greg Brockman, Palantir ( PLTR ) CEO Alex Karp, Amazon ( AMZN ) founder Jeff Bezos, and others.
